top_hackathons.name: CODERAVE 2.0
top_hackathons.tagline: CODE • COLLABORATE • INNOVATE - The SLIET Annual  Hackathon.
top_hackathons.description:
# CODERAVE 2.0
## National-Level Hybrid Hackathon
**Organized by Internwell SLIET Club**  
**Venue:** Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab  
**Mode:** Hybrid — Online (All India) + Offline (SLIET Campus)

### About the Hackathon
Coderave 2.0 is a national-level hybrid hackathon designed to bring together innovative minds, passionate developers, designers, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful technology solutions.

Organized by Internwell SLIET Club, this edition offers students an opportunity to demonstrate their creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities through a competitive, time-bound development experience.

The hackathon welcomes teams from colleges and universities across India through its online participation track, while SLIET students can participate in the offline campus track. Shortlisted teams will present their ideas through PPT pitches, followed by an intensive 24-hour open-source development challenge in which participants will build, test, and demonstrate their solutions.

Whether you are interested in web development, app development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, or other emerging technologies, Coderave 2.0 is your platform to innovate, collaborate, and compete.

### Participation Tracks

**1. Online Track — All India**
- Open to eligible student teams from colleges and universities across India.
- Register online and submit your project proposal PPT.
- A maximum of 20 teams(not confirm) will be shortlisted nationally for the online track.
- Shortlisted teams will pitch their PPT to the judges through an online meeting platform or offline.
- Selected teams(only 5 team) will participate in the 24-hour development challenge remotely, from their preferred location.
- Finalists will submit their source code repository, project documentation, and demo video for evaluation.
- Online participants may be invited to attend the offline campus event if feasible and communicated by the organizers.

**2. Offline Track — SLIET Campus**
- Open to eligible students of SLIET, Longowal.
- Register online and submit the project proposal PPT during registration.
- Shortlisted teams will present their PPT in person on campus on 13 February.
- The offline 24-hour hackathon(both online and offline track ) will begin at 5:00 PM on 13 February and conclude at 5:00 PM on 14 February.
- Teams will develop and demonstrate their solutions according to the official rules and submission instructions.

### Team Formation and Eligibility
- Minimum team size: 3 members.
- Maximum team size: 6 members.
- Each team must include at least 1 girl member(max 3 girls).
- One member must be designated as the Team Leader.
- **The Team Leader will complete the registration on behalf of the entire team and provide accurate details for every member.**
- Each participant may belong to only one registered team.
- All team members must meet the eligibility requirements announced by the organizers.

### Registration and Selection Process
**Round 1 — Registration and PPT Submission:** The Team Leader registers the complete team and submits the project proposal PPT.

**Round 2 — PPT Evaluation and Shortlisting:** Judges evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and presentation quality.

**Round 3 — PPT Pitch:** Shortlisted online teams(Max 20 team) pitch through an online meeting. Shortlisted SLIET teams pitch offline on campus on 13 February.

**Round 4 — 24-Hour Open-Source Hackathon:** Selected teams(Both online and offline track) build their solutions within the official development window.

**Round 5 — Final Submission and Evaluation:** Teams submit their working solution, source code repository, demo video, and other required deliverables. Judges evaluate the final projects and announce the winners.

**Round 6 — Winner Announce:** To be announce.

### 24-Hour Development Challenge
The hackathon is an opportunity to turn ideas into functional prototypes within 24 hours. Teams are expected to develop their solutions during the official event window and use open-source tools, libraries, and technologies wherever possible.

Participants must maintain a project repository, provide clear documentation, and ensure that their work is demonstrable. Teams must disclose third-party components and follow applicable open-source licences. Previously developed work must be declared, and the core solution must comply with the organizers' originality requirements.

### Prizes, Goodies, and Recognition
Exciting prizes, goodies, certificates, and recognition await outstanding teams. Final awards, prize amounts, sponsor benefits, and certificate eligibility will be announced through the official event communication.

### Why Participate?
- Compete with innovative student teams from across India.
- Showcase your technical and creative abilities.
- Build a functional prototype under real-world time constraints.
- Receive feedback from judges and industry professionals, where available.
- Strengthen your portfolio and project repository.
- Network with fellow innovators and the technology community.

### Important Dates
- Registration opens: To be announced.
- Registration and PPT submission deadline: To be announced.
- Online PPT pitches: Before 13 February, on a date announced by the organizers.
- Offline SLIET PPT pitches: 13 February.
- Offline 24-hour hackathon: 13 February, 5:00 PM – 14 February, 5:00 PM.
- Final demo and results: To be announce.

**Note:** The dates above are **tentative** until officially confirmed. The year, registration deadline, online pitch schedule, and final evaluation schedule will be published by the organizers.

### Join Coderave 2.0
Bring your idea, build your team, and turn innovation into impact. Register for Coderave 2.0 and take your first step toward creating something extraordinary.

**Organized by Internwell SLIET Club**  
Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab.

top_hackathons.name: ECLIPSE 7.0
top_hackathons.description:
> # **All that you need to know about Eclipse 7.0**

**ECLIPSE 7.0** is the flagship event of the ACM Student Chapter, TIET, and a premier **24-hour hackathon** that draws participation from across the nation. As the chapter’s most distinguished and celebrated initiative, it serves as a dynamic platform for developers, designers, and innovators to collaborate and compete.
With expert-led workshops, dedicated mentorship, and an intense build environment, **ECLIPSE 7.0** is designed to cultivate innovation, enhance technical excellence, and transform ambitious ideas into impactful, real-world solutions.

> **Eligibility:**

• The hackathon is open to students from all Colleges and Universities.

• Students from all academic years are eligible to participate. Teams may include members from different colleges.

• Participants from diverse specializations are welcome to form teams together.

> **Team Format:**

**Teams must consist of 2–5 members.**
Participants are advised to form teams with complementary expertise, including design, frontend development, backend development, and database management.

> **Problem Statements:**

Each team must choose only ONE problem statement.
The detailed problem statements will be published in the PDF below and simultaneously made accessible on the ECLIPSE 7.0 website and ACM’s official social media platforms.

> **Rounds & Duration:**

**Round 1:** Pre-Screening Round (Online): Teams will be shortlisted based on their idea presentation.

 

**Round 2:** Offline Hackathon Round: Shortlisted teams will participate in the on-site hackathon.

During the offline round, teams will be assessed at regular checkpoints to ensure consistent progress.
All rounds must be completed within the officially communicated timelines.

> **Attendance:**

Physical attendance at the venue is mandatory for all qualifying participants.

> **Required submissions for the offline round include:**

A code repository link and/or deployed project link and a project proposal document

> **Rules:**

• Teams must register exclusively through Devfolio and provide accurate team and member details.

• Teams will be evaluated only on the problem statement they have selected. Working on multiple problem statements is strictly prohibited.

• The prototype must be developed strictly during the offline round. Pre-built solutions will result in disqualification.

• Plagiarism is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification.

• All submissions must be original.

• All participants are required to join the official event application and community platform. Failure to comply may result in disqualification.

• Participants must strictly follow the Code of Conduct throughout the event.

• Any form of misconduct or rule violation may result in disqualification at the discretion of the organizing committee.

• Projects will be evaluated by a panel of judges. The decision of the judges will be final and binding.

top_hackathons.name: ETHChiangmai & Longevity Hackathon 2026
top_hackathons.description:
ETHChiangmai & Longevity Hackathon 2026 brings together builders from Web3, AI and Longevity in Chiang Mai on December 26–27. Over two days, teams of 1–4 will build real products for real people, from stablecoin payments used by local merchants to tools that help people sleep, move and live better.

Total Prize Pool: 10,000 USDT across four tracks

PayFi & RWA (3,000 USDT): bring stablecoins and onchain assets into everyday life: payments, crypto cards, merchant acceptance, remittances, real-world assets, and agentic payments.
Longevity (3,000 USDT): an open, product-focused track with no Web3 requirement. Build around movement, sleep, biohacking and peptides, including AI health companions.
Privacy & Data Sovereignty (3,000 USDT): give people real ownership of their data through ZK, FHE, private identity, health data sovereignty and private AI.
Cosmo-Localism (Bonus, 1,000 USDT): build for real users in Southeast Asia. It can be combined with any other track.

AI is welcome in every track, and any tech stack is welcome.

Whether you’re a developer, designer, researcher or health enthusiast, come build with a global community in one of the world’s favourite cities for digital nomads.

https://ethchiangmai.com/

top_hackathons.description:
# DEVNEXUS
**Connecting developers and innovation**

DEVNEXUS is a 6-hour hackathon organized by SATI Coding Club, primarily aimed at university students who are passionate about technology, creativity, and innovation.

The event is designed to empower students by providing them with a platform to enhance their technical skills, develop problem-solving abilities, explore emerging technologies, and transform innovative ideas into practical solutions.

Through teamwork, collaboration, and hands-on development, participants will get an opportunity to think beyond traditional classroom learning, gain practical experience, and connect with like-minded innovators from different academic backgrounds.

DEVNEXUS encourages students to experiment, learn, build, and challenge their creative limits while fostering a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, and technological advancement.

Join us for 6 hours of learning, building, networking, and creating something meaningful.

**Connect. Collaborate. Create. Build What's Next.**
